text:
To abolish synthesis of the anti-nutritional compound you want a mutation that knocks out (strongly inactivates) the protein very early in its coding sequence.  
The surest way is to introduce a premature stop codon near the start of the open-reading frame; this will give a very short, non-functional peptide and the mRNA is likely to be degraded by nonsense‐mediated decay.

Examine the first few codons of each mutant (codons are spaced for clarity, translation starts with ATG):

Intact gene  
ATG TTT CTC GCT GGT … (Met-Phe-Leu-Ala-Gly-…)

Mutant 1  
ATG TTC TAC GCT GGT …  (no stop; only a couple of amino-acid substitutions)

Mutant 2  
ATG TTC TAA GCT GGT …  
Here the third codon is TAA – an in-frame stop codon. Translation would terminate after only two amino acids, destroying gene function.

Mutant 3  
ATG TTT TAC GCT GGT … (still in frame, no early stop)

Mutant 4  
ATG TTT TAC GCT ACT … (still in frame, no early stop)

Only Mutant 2 introduces an early nonsense (stop) mutation, making it overwhelmingly the most likely to abolish production of the enzyme that synthesises the anti-nutritional compound.

Answer: D
